sound.summary: Plays a sound at a point, for whoever is close enough to hear it. With no arguments, the sounds that exist.
params: optional: also how far it reaches, `1` by default
sound.returns: `list` of the names with no arguments, `num` of the players who heard it otherwise.
examples: effect.sound();   // every sound the game knows

signatures: particle(name, pos, how_many, spread, speed, player)
particle.summary: Spawns particles at a point. With no arguments, the particles that exist.
params: the particle, as `'flame'`; it takes parameters too, `'dust 1 0 0 1'`
optional: how many, one by default
optional: how far around the point they scatter
optional: only that player sees them
particle.returns: `list` of the names with no arguments, `null` otherwise.
examples: effect.particle('dust 1 0 0 1', pos, 10, 0.3, 0, player);   // only for them

particle_line.summary: A line of particles between two points.
params: optional: how many particles per block
optional: only that player sees it

particle_box.summary: The twelve edges of a box in particles - the quick way to show the area a script is working on.
params: optional: how many particles per block
optional: only that player sees it
particle_box.note: For something that stays and takes colours there is `draw_shape` in `core.mc.shape`; this one costs nothing and needs no client.

post_effect.summary: The post-processing shaders of one or more players - what the game calls `/posteffect`.
params: a player or a list of players
post_effect.returns: `num` of the players changed, or `list` of the active effects for `'list'`.
post_effect.note: It goes through the same packet as the vanilla command, so it works on any client and survives a trip out of the world and back. It has no duration: it is removed explicitly.
